title: 'Business as usual' for PSG despite Kvaratskhelia injury
subtitle: Paris Saint-Germain overcame Barcelona 4-2 in the Champions League, but they suffered several injury blows.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique says it is "business as usual" for Paris Saint-Germain, despite Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's serious injury.
Kvaratskhelia faces a long spell out after he suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona in the Champions League.
Ousmane Dembele was also a casualty in that win, with last year's Ballon d'Or winner now expected to miss several weeks. Marquinhos also sustained an issue against Barca.
PSG host Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash on Monday, with the clash pushed back a day due to ongoing protests in the French capital.
However, Luis Enrique insisted PSG will not be altering how they approach games due to their absences.
"It will be business as usual. I don't want to change anything I've done, but I also want to change," Luis Enrique told reporters.
"That's what you have to do to remain unpredictable. It depends on the team and the time of year.
"It's true that losing three players in the same game is strange. It's a motivation for us as a team. We're moving on to improve."
Asked about Kvaratskhelia's state of mind, Luis Enrique said: "It's a tough injury. You think about the player, what he's going to go through. It's difficult, but you have to stay positive.

"When you're a professional player and you want to have a 10-15 year career, you have to have injuries. You have to try to find positive things, and there will be some. He is and will be very important for us.

"It's a risk to be a professional player. You have to accept the positive and negative things, that's life. You have to overcome this to show what kind of player he is. We'll see after the operation. He'll come back stronger, I have no doubt."
Lyon, the current league leaders, have 14 points from seven Ligue 1 matches this season.
This is the joint-fewest points total for a leader at this stage in the three-points-for-a-win era (since 1994-95), level with Lyon and Paris SG in 1999-00, Nice in 2002-03, and Monaco in 2023-24.
With Kvaratskhelia and Doue absent, there will be more onus on Desire Doue to lead PSG's attack, though the youngster is certainly capable of that.
Doue scored against Barca in midweek, and has now been involved in 16 goals in his last 16 Champions League games.
Morton leads Ligue 1 this season for throughballs (eight), ahead of Doue (five).
He has created four chances, too, though the former Liverpool man is yet to provide an assist or score this term.
MATCH PREDICTION: PSG WIN

PSG are the favourites according to Opta's model, but they have lost three of their last six home games against Lyon in Ligue 1 (W3), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 30 such encounters (W18 D9).
The two-time European champions have conceded at least one goal in their last seven Ligue 1 matches against Lyon (10 conceded), their longest current run against a single opponent.
Lyon are top of Ligue 1 at such an advanced stage of the season for the first time since the end of MD19 in 2020-21. PSG were also second behind Lyon at that point.
PSG have scored in their last 52 home Ligue 1 matches (132 goals), since a 0-0 draw against Lorient in Luis Enrique's first game in charge in August 2023.
They could equal the longest such run in the last 50 years, set by Monaco between September 2015 and April 2018 (53).
